equivalents.assumptions: Ordinary Buffer/Uint8Array inputs and standards-conforming async iterators; no proxies, overwritten typed-array methods, concurrent mutation/detachment, private-state reflection or prototype monkey-patching. Observable contract includes returned bytes/count, typed errors, iterator lifecycle and bounded resource ownership; it does not promise identical instruction counts for bounded empty copies. Exact promise-resolution or internal microtask scheduling is not an API guarantee.
equivalents.proof: peek() has already established length <= available. Each iteration copies min(remaining chunk bytes, requested bytes still unwritten), so written cannot exceed length. Once written equals length, any remaining valid queue entries contribute a zero-length subarray and a zero-length set at offset length. The changed OR only visits these extra zero-copy entries; it exits at queue length and does not change state or output. Re-reviewed after introducing the head cursor: the loop begins at headIndex; only indices below headIndex are cleared, so every visited entry remains defined. available equals the sum of active entries from headIndex onward, less headOffset. Prefix compaction preserves their order and these invariants. The original reasoning therefore continues to apply to the active suffix.

equivalents.proof: On failure, the catch block explicitly assigns failed = true regardless of its initial value. On success, countFrames returns only after observing end of input with no buffered bytes; reader.close has no iterator.return to invoke and cannot fail. Initializing failed to true merely routes this already-idempotent successful cleanup through the try/catch branch.

equivalents.proof: A successful count returns only after has() observes EOF and proves no bytes remain, either after the last frame or when skipFrameBoundaryMetadata returns true. That helper returns true only after EOF, including after final ID3v1; embedded tags return false and traversal continues. skipExactly has consumed and released all queued chunks. The success-only close call is already a no-op on externally owned resources. Short acquisition may read EOF early, but success still consumes all bytes before returning. No reader escapes to callers.

equivalents.proof: tied is read only after the bounded candidate loop. The first qualifying candidate has at least one MPEG header and therefore strictly exceeds initial bestMatches = 0; that branch resets tied = false. Subsequent comparisons do not depend on the initial value. If no candidate qualifies, bestMatches === 0 throws regardless of tied. Metadata evidence only breaks ties after a candidate has already been accepted and does not alter this initialization argument.

equivalents.proof: Both streaming and bounded-probe paths call decodeTagHeader before using hasFooter. It rejects versions outside 2..4 and flags outside 0xc0 for v2.2 or 0xe0 for v2.3; those masks exclude footer bit0x10. Only v2.4 can therefore reach hasFooter with that bit set. Replacing this final version test with true changes neither the header result, streaming skip/footer checks nor probe boundary evidence. Probe catches invalid headers instead of accepting them; it does not bypass validation. The short-inference prefix probe validates every available header byte with the same decoder. An incomplete valid prefix returns undefined before constructing hasFooter; any returned TagHeader therefore has ten validated bytes. Missing version/flag completion witnesses cannot bypass the final complete-header guard or produce a footer for v2.2/v2.3.

equivalents.assumptions: Ordinary Buffer/Uint8Array inputs. Out-of-range typed-array reads return undefined; isEncoderFrame receives a decoded MPEG-1 Layer III header and a view of exactly that frame's span from count-frames, or a test-constructed complete frame. The observable contract is the boolean result.
equivalents.proof: If the signature would extend past the frame, at least one compared index is out of range and reads as undefined, which never equals a character code, so every() returns false exactly as the guard does.

equivalents.proof: The results differ only when a four-byte signature ends exactly at the frame end. Every caller then needs more bytes: xingAt returns false at position + 8 > frame.length, and vbriAt at position + 26 > frame.length. isEncoderFrame therefore returns false either way.

equivalents.proof: As in EQ-VBR-U32-SUBTRACT-C, write the sum as 256 * K + d with K = 65536a - 256b + c, which lies in (-2^24, 2^24). Validation passes only if K = 0, so 65536a + c = 256b. Because 256b <= 65280, a = 0, so c = 256b and therefore b = c = 0. The validated flags equal the original d; all other inputs are rejected by both.

equivalents.proof: unsigned32 feeds only (flags & ~0x0f) === 0 and then the low four bits. Write the sum as 256 * K + d with K = 65536a + 256b - c in [-255, 2^24). After >>> 0 the high 24 bits are K mod 2^24, so validation passes only if K = 0, which forces a = b = c = 0, and the value is then d, as in the original. Every other input is rejected by both. An exhaustive byte-level check found no difference.

equivalents.proof: Every consumed head is cleared before headIndex advances. Replacing the empty-queue fast-path condition with false leaves an empty active suffix with headIndex equal to queued.length. A later non-empty input is pushed at that exact index, so the next active head is unchanged. The remaining threshold branch still compacts whenever 1024 consumed entries accumulate, including when the suffix is empty. All bytes, offsets, lifecycle calls and error paths are unchanged; live slots remain bounded by active chunks plus at most 1023 consumed slots. This only defers empty-array compaction.

equivalents.proof: The empty-queue branch is unchanged. For a nonempty active suffix, forcing the compaction condition true removes only cleared prefix entries and resets headIndex to zero. splice preserves the active chunks and their order; headOffset has the same value after the surrounding consume step. Immediate compaction after each completed chunk therefore preserves every public cursor result and retains no additional payload references. Live slot storage is no larger than the original. The additional bounded copying cost is outside the promised functional and memory contract and is assessed by performance measurements separately.

equivalents.proof: Changing >=1024 to >1024 delays nonempty-prefix compaction by one completed chunk. Consumed entries are still cleared immediately. Before either compaction, indexing starts at headIndex and available describes precisely the active suffix; afterward the same active suffix is moved to index zero. The public results, ownership and exceptions are identical, and at most one additional undefined slot is retained. Both variants have a constant storage bound independent of total stream length.

equivalents.assumptions: Ordinary Buffer/Uint8Array inputs and standards-conforming async iterators; no private-state reflection, prototype monkey-patching or concurrent mutation. equivalents.proof: headIndex starts at zero. With the mutated <1024 comparison, the first completed chunk increments it to one. If the queue empties, the unchanged empty branch resets it to zero; otherwise one is below 1024, so compaction removes the cleared prefix and resets it to zero. Induction gives the same reset on every later completed chunk. Thus this exact mutant performs eager nonempty compaction, equivalent to EQ-QUEUE-EAGER-COMPACTION for bytes, offsets, errors, lifecycle and bounded storage. It cannot reach the apparent no-compaction state at headIndex>=1024 under a single-mutant execution.

When end exceeds the fixed probe length, the original breaks after appending the current frame descriptor. Without that early guard, probeMetadata(window, end) inspects only empty subarrays and returns the same offset, zero tags and canEnd=true; neither ID3 signature can match. Adding zero tags does not change metadataMatches or anchored. The offset is strictly beyond, not equal to, the probe end, so the EOF branch is not taken. headerAt then returns undefined at its offset+4>length guard and the loop terminates. The returned base, frame descriptors, matches, anchored and metadataMatches are identical. Candidate positions and spans are bounded finite nonnegative integers. No reader method, iterator operation or payload decoder is invoked on the extra path. It allocates only a fixed number of temporary empty views within the already bounded candidate loop; retained input, lookahead, cursor movement and resource ownership do not change.

equivalents.proof: This return is reached only after atEnd is true or a complete final ID3v1 has been skipped, and after reader.has(1) has returned false. The reader is therefore at zero available bytes with its iterator-done state cached. countFrames calls this helper only after at least one MPEG frame. Returning false instead of true makes countFrames continue once: its has(4) returns false from cached EOF, validateFrameSequenceEnd observes frames>0 and its has(1) also returns false, then traversal returns the identical frames-minus-excludedEncoderFrame value. Neither has call invokes the iterator, consumes bytes or allocates a larger buffer; the offset and typed error behavior are unchanged. The same finally block closes the reader once; cached completion prevents an additional iterator.return call. The only difference is bounded control flow and internal promise scheduling after EOF, which is not part of the public contract.

equivalents.proof: The private decoder has two strict callers, readTagHeader and probeTagEnvelope, which prove a complete ten-byte header before calling. Its only incomplete-input caller is hasPossibleMetadataPrefix, which observes metadata plausibility, not the returned header or size. For a still-plausible prefix shorter than ten bytes, every available size byte has already passed the synchsafe check. Missing size bytes coerce to zero in the bounded bitwise size expression, so bodyLength remains nonnegative. A computed footer begins at least ten bytes from the prefix start, beyond all available bytes; its supplied footer view is empty and matchesFooterPrefix returns true. Without a footer the other branch likewise returns true. The original undefined result also returns true immediately. Invalid prefixes still throw at the same earlier validation and become false in the same caller. No reader method, iterator operation, cursor, propagated error, returned count or resource ownership changes. Only a fixed local header object and bounded arithmetic are added; neither retained-input size nor asymptotic memory/work bounds change.
